title.narrative: Engendered livelihood governance: Toward a more consolidated approach

description.narrative: Women farmers encounter in their work various difficulties among which: no access to quality seeds, fertilizers necessary for their farming activities, problems related to the lack of knowledge of new techniques, problems of transformation of agricultural products, of evacuation and market access of products, problem of farm income management, just to name a few. And yet, the work of these women contributes to food insecurity. If their activities were growing more and more, they would help to combat food insecurity for a large part of the population, especially the poor populations living in the outlying and densely populated neighbourhoods of the city. This project is to prepare women to change their vision of individual work into a new approach that is more cohesive envisioning a "kind of social economy enterprise" co-operative based on benefit sharing and risk reduction for the development of members of the Cooperative. This involves the work of awareness, persuasion to arrive at the change towards "associative spirit". To do this, they will have to benefit from capacity strengthening on this issue in order to understand the usefulness of a cooperative. The project will also help to strengthen their capacity with access to information on tax, market access and market status for some of the agricultural products.
